hits.vignette: A 5-month-old boy has dilated cardiomyopathy, neutropenia, poor growth, and proximal muscle weakness. Urine testing shows increased 3-methylglutaconic acid. His maternal uncle died in infancy of heart failure. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic variant in TAFAZZIN.
hits.lead_in: The affected protein normally performs which of the following functions?
hits.tested_construct: TAFAZZIN encodes tafazzin, an inner-mitochondrial-membrane phospholipid transacylase required for remodeling immature cardiolipin into mature cardiolipin species. Defective cardiolipin remodeling disrupts mitochondrial membrane organization and respiratory-chain function, producing the X-linked Barth syndrome phenotype.

hits.vignette: A 74-year-old retired teacher comes for a routine health visit. She lives alone, manages her finances and medications, drives without difficulty, and volunteers at a library twice weekly. During the past 2 years, she has noticed that she sometimes needs more time to recall the names of acquaintances, although the names usually come to her later. Her family has not noticed repetitive questioning, getting lost, or changes in judgment. Neurologic examination is normal.
hits.lead_in: Compared with a healthy 25-year-old adult, which of the following patterns on cognitive testing is most consistent with normal aging in this patient?
hits.tested_construct: Age-associated changes in cognitive processing and retrieval without pathologic loss of stored semantic knowledge or functional independence

hits.vignette: A 7-year-old boy is evaluated for recurrent respiratory infections and poor weight gain. He has had several episodes of bacterial sinusitis and pneumonia. His stools are bulky and foul-smelling. Physical examination shows digital clubbing. Sweat chloride concentration is elevated, and genetic testing identifies pathogenic variants in CFTR.
hits.lead_in: Which of the following cellular abnormalities most directly contributes to the formation of thick airway secretions in this patient?
hits.tested_construct: Loss of CFTR-mediated epithelial chloride transport impairs water movement and dehydrates mucus

hits.vignette: A healthy 11-year-old girl begins breast development followed several months later by a rapid increase in height. She has no chronic illness and takes no medications.
hits.lead_in: Which physiologic change most directly initiates normal activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis at puberty?
hits.tested_construct: Increasing pulsatile hypothalamic GnRH secretion stimulates pituitary LH and FSH release and activates gonadal steroid production during puberty.

hits.vignette: A 14-year-old boy with sickle cell disease develops severe pain in both legs after prolonged exercise and dehydration. Peripheral blood smear shows sickled erythrocytes.
hits.lead_in: Which molecular event most directly causes the acute erythrocyte deformation in this patient?
hits.tested_construct: Deoxygenated hemoglobin S polymerizes because a beta-globin glutamate-to-valine substitution creates a hydrophobic interaction, deforming erythrocytes and promoting vaso-occlusion.

hits.vignette: A 22-year-old man develops jaundice and dark urine 2 days after receiving an oxidant medication. Blood smear shows bite cells and Heinz-body-associated damage.
hits.lead_in: Deficiency of which metabolic product most directly increases this patient's erythrocyte susceptibility to oxidative stress?
hits.tested_construct: G6PD deficiency lowers pentose-phosphate-pathway NADPH generation, impairing maintenance of reduced glutathione and increasing erythrocyte susceptibility to oxidative injury.

hits.vignette: A 12-year-old boy has chronic mild jaundice, splenomegaly, and anemia. His father underwent splenectomy for a similar disorder. Peripheral smear shows numerous spherocytes.
hits.lead_in: Which diagnosis best explains this patient's findings?
hits.tested_construct: Defects in erythrocyte membrane-cytoskeletal proteins reduce membrane stability and surface area, producing poorly deformable spherocytes that are trapped and destroyed in the spleen.

hits.vignette: A 19-year-old woman has recurrent epistaxis, easy bruising, and prolonged bleeding after dental procedures. Her mother has similar symptoms. Platelet count is normal.
hits.lead_in: Which diagnosis best explains this pattern of bleeding?
hits.tested_construct: Quantitative or qualitative deficiency of von Willebrand factor impairs platelet adhesion and reduces stabilization of coagulation factor VIII.

hits.vignette: An 8-year-old boy has recurrent hemarthroses after minor trauma. His maternal uncle had similar episodes. Platelet count and prothrombin time are normal, and activated partial thromboplastin time is prolonged.
hits.lead_in: Which coagulation protein is most likely deficient?
hits.tested_construct: Factor VIII deficiency impairs the intrinsic tenase complex, reducing activation of factor X and thrombin generation during secondary hemostasis.

hits.vignette: A 32-year-old woman with heavy menstrual bleeding has fatigue and pica. Hemoglobin is 9.1 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume is 70 fL, serum ferritin is low, and total iron-binding capacity is elevated.
hits.lead_in: Which diagnosis best explains these findings?
hits.tested_construct: Iron depletion limits heme synthesis, producing progressively microcytic hypochromic erythrocytes with low ferritin and increased iron-binding capacity.

hits.vignette: A 66-year-old man has fatigue, paresthesias, and impaired vibration sense. Laboratory studies show macrocytic anemia and hypersegmented neutrophils.
hits.lead_in: Which metabolite is most likely elevated because of this vitamin deficiency?
hits.tested_construct: Vitamin B12 deficiency impairs methionine synthase and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase reactions, producing defective DNA synthesis and accumulation of methylmalonic acid with neurologic injury.

hits.vignette: A 6-year-old boy has recurrent deep abscesses caused by Staphylococcus aureus and Aspergillus species. Dihydrorhodamine testing shows minimal fluorescence after neutrophil stimulation.
hits.lead_in: Which cellular function is most directly impaired?
hits.tested_construct: Defective phagocyte NADPH oxidase prevents an effective respiratory burst and superoxide generation, impairing intracellular killing of selected bacteria and fungi.

hits.vignette: An 11-month-old boy has recurrent otitis media and pneumonia beginning at 7 months of age. Tonsils are very small. Laboratory studies show nearly absent circulating B cells and markedly reduced concentrations of all immunoglobulin classes.
hits.lead_in: Which developmental process is defective?
hits.tested_construct: BTK deficiency arrests B-cell maturation at the pre-B-cell stage, causing markedly reduced mature B cells and all immunoglobulin classes after maternal IgG wanes.

hits.vignette: A 4-month-old infant has persistent oral candidiasis, recurrent pneumonia, chronic diarrhea, and failure to thrive. Lymphocyte count is profoundly decreased, and testing shows adenosine deaminase deficiency.
hits.lead_in: Accumulation of which substrate most directly contributes to lymphocyte toxicity?
hits.tested_construct: ADA deficiency causes accumulation of toxic purine metabolites, including deoxyadenosine-derived nucleotides, which are particularly toxic to developing lymphocytes and cause severe combined immunodeficiency.

hits.vignette: A newborn is found to have microcytosis. Genetic testing shows deletion of three alpha-globin genes.
hits.lead_in: Which abnormal hemoglobin is most likely to be prominent after birth in this patient?
hits.tested_construct: Deletion or inactivation of alpha-globin genes reduces alpha-chain production, causing excess beta-like chains and severity proportional to the number of affected alpha-globin alleles.

hits.vignette: A 29-year-old woman has painful loss of vision in one eye that improves over several weeks. Eight months later she develops numbness of the left leg and urinary urgency. Examination shows hyperreflexia in the left leg.
hits.lead_in: Which diagnosis best explains this pattern?
hits.tested_construct: Immune-mediated central nervous system demyelination produces neurologic deficits separated in time and space, often including optic neuritis, sensory symptoms, and upper motor neuron findings.

hits.vignette: A 68-year-old man has progressive bradykinesia, resting tremor, rigidity, and reduced arm swing while walking.
hits.lead_in: Loss of neurons in which structure most directly causes this disorder?
hits.tested_construct: Degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta reduces striatal dopamine, decreasing direct-pathway activity and increasing indirect-pathway influence on movement.

hits.vignette: A 38-year-old man develops progressive chorea, irritability, and impaired executive function. His father developed similar symptoms at age 52.
hits.lead_in: Which genetic change best explains the earlier onset in this patient?
hits.tested_construct: Expansion of a CAG trinucleotide repeat in HTT produces a toxic polyglutamine-expanded huntingtin protein and autosomal dominant neurodegeneration with anticipation.

hits.vignette: A 31-year-old woman has ptosis and diplopia that worsen late in the day and improve after rest. Sensation and reflexes are normal.
hits.lead_in: The most common antibodies in this disorder target which structure?
hits.tested_construct: Autoantibodies most often target postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, reducing functional receptor density and producing fatigable skeletal-muscle weakness.

hits.vignette: A 44-year-old man develops diplopia, dysphagia, dry mouth, and progressive descending weakness 18 hours after eating home-canned vegetables. He is afebrile and sensation is intact.
hits.lead_in: Which diagnosis is most likely?
hits.tested_construct: Botulinum neurotoxin blocks presynaptic acetylcholine release at peripheral cholinergic synapses, producing cranial neuropathies followed by symmetric descending flaccid paralysis.

hits.vignette: A 35-year-old man develops tingling in his feet followed over 3 days by symmetric ascending leg weakness. Two weeks earlier he had a diarrheal illness. Deep-tendon reflexes are absent.
hits.lead_in: Which diagnosis best explains these findings?
hits.tested_construct: Acute immune-mediated peripheral nerve injury, often after infection, causes rapidly progressive symmetric weakness with hyporeflexia or areflexia and can impair respiratory muscles.
